text:
Driftline can now open the fix for you.

Add fix-pr: true to the GitHub Action and you get one draft pull request that renames retiring model IDs, kept up to date until you merge. Lines a rename can't fix get a checklist with the provider's guide.
aidriftline.com/#pr

{retiring90} AI model IDs retire in the next 90 days across OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral, xAI, Groq, Cohere, DeepSeek, Bedrock, Vertex AI and Azure.

Find the ones in your code, no install and no key:
npx -y @aidriftline/driftline .

A rename keeps the API call working. The answers can still change.

Driftline Pro runs your real prompts on the old and the new model and puts a verdict in the fix pull request: safe to merge, read first, or don't merge yet.
aidriftline.com/#drift

Retirement alerts for any AI model now go to Slack, Discord or any webhook, as well as email.

Open the model's page, paste the webhook link, and you get a post 30 days before, 7 days before and on the day.
aidriftline.com/models/

Next fixed retirement: {next_id} on {next_date}, {next_days} days from now.

Check whether it's in your code:
npx -y @aidriftline/driftline .

Alerts by email, Slack or webhook: aidriftline.com/models/{next_id}/

Where do Driftline's retirement dates come from? From the providers' own pages, checked every 6 hours.

Every source and when it was last read, in public: aidriftline.com/status/

Coding agents write model IDs from their training data, and many of those are already retired.

Driftline's MCP server lets Claude Code, Cursor or Copilot check an ID before writing it:
claude mcp add driftline -- npx -y @aidriftline/driftline mcp

Swap retiring model IDs in one command:
npx @aidriftline/driftline fix --dry-run

It changes only lines where the new name is the whole change. The rest is listed with the reason: new parameters, a different API, or two possible replacements.

The same Claude or Gemini model can retire on different dates at Anthropic, Bedrock, Vertex AI and Azure.

Driftline reads how your code calls the model and uses that platform's own date, per region on Bedrock.
aidriftline.com/models/bedrock/

Driftline findings can sit in GitHub code scanning next to your other alerts.

Set sarif-file in the Action and upload the file with github/codeql-action/upload-sarif. Free on public repositories.
github.com/AI-Driftline/driftline

How many prompts should you test before switching models? 5 to 20: the ones your app really sends.

Driftline Pro makes two API calls per prompt on your own key, scores the difference, and fails hard when a JSON answer stops parsing.
aidriftline.com/#drift

Driftline's scan is free, with no account and no key: GitHub Action, CLI and MCP server.

{total} model IDs from 8 providers and 3 clouds, each with the replacement its provider recommends.
github.com/AI-Driftline/driftline

Word overlap can't tell "is eligible" from "is not eligible".

In .driftline/prompts.yml, add must_include and must_not_include to a prompt. If the new model's answer fails a check, the prompt is marked broken.
github.com/AI-Driftline/driftline#checks

Your prompt returns JSON? Add same_fields: [status, total, customer.id].

Those fields must keep the current model's value on the replacement, or the prompt is marked broken. Dots reach nested fields.
github.com/AI-Driftline/driftline#checks

Not every replacement is a rename. Driftline labels each one: Rename, Parameter changes, API change, Re-embed data, Pick one of two, or Fewer features.

The label and the provider's guide are on every model page.
aidriftline.com/models/

When a provider's page and Driftline's registry disagree, the model is marked "under review" and its alerts wait. You never get a date that might be wrong.

See what is under review right now:
aidriftline.com/status/

Some retirements don't switch the model off. Google routes old Gemini IDs to a newer model, and xAI and DeepSeek often redirect too.

The call keeps working and the answers change, so Driftline flags these as well.
aidriftline.com/models/

Moving from Claude 4.6 or older to 4.7 or later? If your code sets temperature, top_p or top_k, remove them. Those models accept only the defaults.

Find the old Claude IDs:
npx -y @aidriftline/driftline .

Moving to a new embedding model? Vectors from different models can't be compared.

Re-embed your stored data with the new model, query with that same model, and check the vector size: it may differ.
npx -y @aidriftline/driftline .

Choose when the build fails. In the Action, fail-on takes retired, at-risk or never, and warn-days sets what counts as retiring soon (default 90).

Start with fail-on: never and read the report first.
github.com/AI-Driftline/driftline

Put one rule in AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md: run npx -y @aidriftline/driftline . --json before choosing a model ID, and never add one marked retired or at-risk.

A ready-made snippet:
aidriftline.com/agents/

{retiring30} AI model IDs retire in the next 30 days, {retiring90} in the next 90.

The next fixed date is {next_date}: {next_id}.

See whether any of them are in your repository:
npx -y @aidriftline/driftline .

Driftline tracks {total} model IDs across 8 providers, Bedrock, Vertex AI and Azure, each with the replacement its provider names. Cloud platforms keep their own dates.

Browse them all:
aidriftline.com/models/

On 14 Jan 2027 OpenAI retires gpt-4o-2024-08-06, gpt-4o-2024-11-20, gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18, gpt-4.1-2025-04-14 and gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14. OpenAI's replacement for all five is gpt-6-luna.

aidriftline.com/models/gpt-4o-2024-08-06/

On 26 Feb 2027 OpenAI retires whisper-1 and the gpt-4o transcribe models. OpenAI names gpt-transcribe for recorded files and gpt-live-transcribe for live audio.

Word timestamps and subtitles work differently, so check them.
aidriftline.com/models/whisper-1/
